toBe vs toEqual vs toMatchObject for objects?
a: toBe: the very same object in memory (almost never what you want). toEqual: all keys and values equal. toMatchObject: at least these keys/values, extra keys allowed.

q: type vs interface: when do you use which?
a: Both describe object shapes. type can also describe unions and function types and uses =. interface is objects only, no =, common for page objects/classes. Be consistent in a project.

q: `const copy = original; copy.stock = 0;` Why did original.stock change too? Fix?
a: = doesn't copy an object: both names point to the same object. Make a real copy: const copy = { ...original };

q: In `const { username: login } = account;` what does the colon mean?
a: Rename: take username and store it in a variable called login. Inside destructuring on the LEFT of =, the colon is NOT a type annotation.
